I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over 30 years. My father farmed it before me. I know what works here — the soil, the rains, the market. I'm not going to try anything new that might fail and leave me short of money for winter.

**My thinking:**

My land is about 10 mu, all flat, on the North China Plain. The only sensible rotation here is winter wheat then summer maize on the same ground — everyone in the village does it, the seed dealers stock it, the grain station buys it. I've done this my whole life.

For wheat, I'll plant Ji wheat — the improved variety the township agricultural office has been promoting for years. Better yield than the old seed, not too expensive. I apply fertilizer generously at planting and again at jointing — I'd rather put a bit extra than risk a thin crop. I'll irrigate three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once when the grain is filling. I use a rotary tiller after maize harvest to prepare the seedbed.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June, no-till, to save time. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid — reliable, the seed shop always has it. One big fertilizer application at planting, one topdress at jointing. Two irrigations if the summer rains don't come.

I won't try cotton — the price has been bad. I won't try vegetables — I'm getting older and they take too much bending work. Wheat and maize. Simple, steady.
